page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture using the Neoverse-V2 model, running at 2.7 GHz with no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with read-only small block, read-only large block, and write large block operations all placing in the top 10% tier. Single-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, perform in the middle 50% average tier. In application-specific tests, the instance achieves top-tier results in PassMark database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, while showing weaker performance in small-model LLM prompt processing.

From a resource density perspective, the m8gd.48xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that scale horizontally across its 192 physical cores and require substantial local NVMe storage. The inclusion of 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage reduces the need for external block storage attachments. However, a key tradeoff is the moderate single-core performance, which may limit efficiency for single-threaded tasks, and the absence of hardware GPU accelerators, which restricts its utility for intensive machine learning training.

This instance is configured for large-scale multi-threaded workloads, high-throughput database operations, and memory-intensive applications. Appropriate workloads include distributed databases, Redis caching layers, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-model LLM prompt processing.
